nearest_prior_work: Kakeya (1914) initiated the study of sets of subseries sums and established the compact-set setting for absolutely convergent series.
Modern achievement-set literature uses `achievement set' or `set of subsums' for all 0-1 subseries sums of an absolutely summable sequence.
No primary source was located for the card's exact Mersenne-floor defect Delta_d or its saturated divisor-hole consumer.
classification.attribution: Attribute the achievement-set and compactness background to Kakeya and the later subsum-set literature. Describe the displayed O((Delta_d+|D_d|)/4^d) implication as an elementary scaled-remainder estimate. Credit the local programme only for the Four-Ninths quotient bridge and the exact divisor-hole boundary.
classification.mathematical_interest: The abstract estimate is elementary; the useful content is architectural. It turns two difficult arithmetic inequalities into explicitly named producers feeding a trivial but exact convergence consumer.
classification.reusable_scope: Finite-support approximations in which a common scale splits every term and target into an integer quotient plus uniformly controlled fractional mass.
classification.why_it_matters: It prevents more effort being spent reproving convergence while exposing the real theorem search: prove the signed defect stays nonnegative and subscale, or rule out the first saturated crossing.

primary_sources.does_not_support: No scaled floor-defect criterion or arithmetic saturation obstruction.

mechanism_comparison.standard_core: If 4^d(S_{D_d}-4/9) is the sum of a bounded fractional-mass term, minus a defect Delta_d, minus a target fractional part, then Delta_d=o(4^d) and |D_d|=o(4^d) imply S_{D_d}->4/9.
mechanism_comparison.local_delta: The Lean development identifies the executable signed remainder with this exact quotient defect and proves that a first upper-window escape from saturation forces a simultaneous divisor hole across the entire selected support.
mechanism_comparison.compactness_boundary: The numerical convergence is already explicit. Closedness of the achievement set is the final standard topological step; no diagonal subsequence or symbolic-dynamics compactness theorem is needed.
mechanism_comparison.significance_boundary: The card is a defensible standalone conditional interface, not a standalone deep compactness theorem and not evidence that either all-depth producer is true.
